title: Fox, the tap dancer, and meeting him on Canal Street
summary: Nash recalls the great tap dancer Fox from Algiers and a recent encounter with him, old and rheumatic, sleeping on a newspaper box.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And after that group get through dancing, always some guy would come in there and could tap dance. Had an old fellow there. I guess he must be now about, I know he's 70 something, they called him Fox. He used to be a great dancer too. He was born and raised over there in Al Jays across the river. Whoever Fox come in there, everybody quit dancing. And they started asking him to dance. I met that guy about four months ago sleeping on the newspaper box on Canal Street. And I knew who he was. And I was a young boy at that time, you know. I mean, when he was dancing. He was a great top dancer. You know his full name?
All I ever knew was Fox. He lived over there in Al Jays.
He was born over there. Well, I bet the people over there would know him. Oh yeah, sure they know him. They know him. And he's one of the old timers, man. He really could dance.
Yeah, he was on Canal Street on a newspaper box. He said, yeah, where you know him? He said, yeah, I had that scar on your eyes.

He said, yeah, I had that scar on your eyes. He said, how'd you know me out? He said, you used to be a great top dancer. He said, that was a swell. He was a swell. He was a swell. Oh yeah, sure they know him. Oh yeah, sure they know him. They know him. And he was one of the old timers. He really could dance. Yeah, he was on Canal Street on a newspaper box. And I came by and I said, sir, fellow, what you named Fox? He said, yeah, where you know him at? I said, sometime way many years ago. I said, there was a thing that made me know you from that scar on your eyes. He said, yeah, I had that scar on your eyes. I said, I was a small boy. He said, how did you know me out? I said, you used to be a great tap dancer. He said, that's right. I said, I remember you danced all down there in the red light district, around the Lebanon Padilla, Franklin Grabbing, and all around some Volkers, and all around Gaskin and Villery. He said, that's right, you sure know. I said, I remember, I said, you was a great tap dancer. He said, but I can't dance now. I said, my legs full of rheumatism. All my bones aches now. I never will dance like that anymore. I remember I was sleeping on newspaper, newspaper box.
